Hi Alex — thanks for the clear asks and timeline. Answers below and attached the vendor questionnaire filled partially for context.

SOC 2: We can provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report under a standard NDA. Our legal team can route the report once the NDA is in place; no redactions are standard practice. If you have a PO or procurement portal, let me know and we can add the NDA link.

Deletion SLAs (high level):
- Operational data (customer objects, prompts, user-provided files): contractual deletion within 30 days of termination or written deletion request.
- Backups/snapshots: Redwood retains incremental backups for disaster recovery for a default 90-day window. For customers requiring shorter windows, we offer contractual controls down to 30 days for an enterprise commitment (we can include in SOW). Backups are encrypted and stored with lifecycle policies; when deletion is triggered, we 1) mark objects for deletion, 2) rotate keys, and 3) purge segments during the next compaction cycle. Note: immediate guaranteed purging of all backup segments on arbitrary timestamps is operationally challenging; we provide contractual commitments on maximum time-to-erase (e.g., 30 days) and key-rotation-based cryptographic erasure as an acceleration mechanism.

Logs/Audit:
- Access logs and audit trails are retained by default for 180 days. We can offer a reduced retention window (e.g., 30/90 days) as a configurable setting for enterprise customers. Logs can be exported to your SIEM for longer retention if required. Logs are logically separated by customer tenancy where feasible.

Next steps: 
1) I attached the questionnaire (Amaya_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) partially filled with references to our SOC 2 and retention summary. Please pass to your security/procurement team.
2) Neha will provide a short technical note on backup lifecycle and cryptographic erasure.
3) If you need the SOC 2 under NDA, send the NDA or I can route ours — whichever you prefer.

Hi Alex — quick technical follow-up as promised with more detail on backups and logs.

Backups / Snapshots:
- Snapshot architecture: We maintain incremental snapshots of customer volumes stored in encrypted object storage. Snapshots are immutable once written but are covered by lifecycle policies that remove older segments after the configured retention window.
- Deletion process: On a certified deletion request, we execute three steps: (1) mark all live customer objects for deletion and purge live storage, (2) flag related snapshot metadata for expedited compaction, and (3) rotate snapshot encryption keys (cryptographic erasure) to render remaining snapshot segments unreadable before they are physically purged during the next compaction sweep.
- Timing: Default snapshot retention is 90 days; with enterprise SOW we can contract 30-day maximum time-to-erase using expedited compaction and key rotation. We estimate the cryptographic erasure step completes immediately on key rotation; physical segment purge completes within the contracted SLA window (up to 30 days in covered SOW).

Logs / Audit Trails:
- Default retention: 180 days for audit/access logs. Logs are partitioned by customer ID; where required, we can enable per-customer shorter retention windows (down to 30 days) and provide an API to request ad-hoc deletes for exportable logs.
- Export/Segregation: If Amaya prefers, we can ship logs to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/EventHub) daily and then delete from our primary store to meet stricter retention.

Caveats / notes:
- Some historic backups may be replicated across DR regions; our deletion process will follow the same key-rotation + compaction across replicas but physical purge timing is still subject to replicated lifecycle.
- For regulated data (PHI), we recommend a combined approach: contractual 30-day deletion SLA, key-rotation-based cryptographic erasure, and export of logs to your SIEM.

If helpful, I can share a short one-pager diagram of the deletion lifecycle and a checklist we use during customer offboarding. Happy to jump on a 20-min call with your security team this week.
